rounds.text: Texel Industries is currently trading at a valuation that fails to reflect its intrinsic worth, as evidenced by a discounted cash flow analysis suggesting an intrinsic value of Rs 87 per share against a market price of Rs 60.2 [E40]. This represents a significant margin of safety of 30.4% [E41], further supported by the fact that the stock trades at a P/E of 18.2x and an EV/EBITDA of 8.19x, both of which sit at a discount to their respective sector benchmarks of 21.43x and 12.25x [E1, E6, E11]. The company has demonstrated a clear ability to improve operational efficiency, evidenced by an operating margin of 10% in the trailing twelve months compared to just 2% three years prior [E26]. While the market currently prices the stock for a modest 5.9% earnings growth, the company has previously demonstrated the capacity for substantial profit expansion, including 33% compounded profit growth over the last three years [E18, E42]. Conceded: the company faces challenges with negative operating cash flow of Rs -2 Cr [E31], a decline in promoter holding [E37], and a lack of dividend payouts [E4, E46]. Despite these headwinds, the business operates within a sector currently experiencing a tailwind, providing a supportive macro backdrop for future performance [E59, E60].
